VN Real Estate Watch — Daily Signal Dashboard

Report Date: Friday, May 29, 2026 Data Vintage: May 26-29, 2026 Agent: VN Real Estate Watch

Executive Summary

Vietnam's real estate market remains in a liquidity-constrained environment with elevated funding costs. Deposit rates have surged to 7-8.5% annually, and bank bond yields have reached 8.5-8.9%, signaling persistent liquidity pressure. The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued directives to rein in rate competition, but structural factors—credit growth outpacing deposits by VND2 quadrillion—continue to pressure the system. Hanoi introduced aggressive anti-speculation measures (3-year resale curb), while Vinhomes launched an innovative gold-for-property scheme to unlock idle household gold. Foreign buyer access continues expanding with HCMC adding 2 more eligible projects. The digital asset regulatory framework for HCMC's International Financial Centre is advancing, targeting 2027 launch.

Recovery Probability: LOW (1-2 Tier 1 signals green, need 3+ for recovery call)

5. Policy & Legal Developments

Anti-Speculation Measures

  • Hanoi 3-Year Resale Curb (May 25, Decision 2636): Buyers of commercial housing in multi-functional urban areas cannot transfer ownership within 3 years of full payment. Early resale only to developer at ≤ original contract price. Targets short-term flipping and prioritizes genuine demand. Covers 132-192M m² of planned floor space across 8 development directions.

International Financial Centre (VIFC) Progress

  • HCMC VIFC Framework: 899-hectare zone spanning both banks of Saigon River, connecting financial district with Thu Thiem. Targeting 2027 market launch. 2026 focus: finalizing licensing frameworks, membership portal, one-stop investor service.
  • Digital Asset Regulation: France-Vietnam partnership supporting legal framework development. EU MiCA regulation as reference model. Vietnam tightening digital asset market management (financial crime, data protection, cybersecurity, fraud).

Housing Law Implementation

  • Foreign Ownership: 2023 Housing Law + Decree 95/2024 continuing to expand access. Foreign entities need valid investment certificates or operating licenses. 30% cap per condo building, 250 landed units max per 10,000-resident area.
  • Land Law 2024 / Housing Law / RE Business Law: Implementation ongoing. No major enforcement updates this cycle.

Stuck Projects (Resolution 170/265/29)

  • 3,338 projects worth $129B: No new progress updates this cycle. Carry-forward from prior reports.
  • Social Housing: 102,633 units completed in 2025 (+2% over target), 226 projects commenced. 737 projects, 701K units target pipeline.

  • FDI maturation: Southern Vietnam industrial property market becoming more competitive. "Land banks losing edge" as FDI shifts toward higher-quality facilities.
  • VSIP Phase 2: $26M industrial park approved for central Vietnam
  • Japanese investment: Nishi-Nippon Railroad planning 22,000 homes in Vietnam by 2035
  • Semiconductor/AI: Qualcomm R&D center in Hanoi signals tech sector deepening

Commercial/Luxury

  • Condotels → Luxury shift: Central Vietnam seeing condotel projects convert to luxury apartments. "End of cash cow era" for condotels.
  • Hospitality M&A: Set to drive 2026 market activity
  • Oversupply risk: Commercial sector still faces absorption challenges

  • Enforcement: Developers must buy back at ≤ original price if early exit needed

9. Forward Assessment

Tier 1 Signal Count

  • Green (✅): 0
  • Flat (⚠️): 2 (Deposit-credit spread, SBV policy signals)
  • Worsening (❌): 1 (Mortgage rate trend)
  • No Update: 2 (Secondary-primary gap, Pink book velocity)

Assessment: 0-2 Tier 1 signals improving. Need 3+ green for 6-9 month recovery call. Current trajectory: stagnation with elevated funding costs.

Recovery Probability Estimate

  • Near-term (3-6 months): LOW — Funding costs elevated, liquidity tight, no policy easing signals
  • Medium-term (6-12 months): LOW-MEDIUM — Depends on deposit-credit gap closing, VIFC framework progress
  • Key triggers to watch:
    1. Deposit rates falling below 6% for 12-month tenors
    2. Credit growth slowing to allow deposit catch-up
    3. Pink book issuance acceleration for 220 stuck HCMC projects
    4. VIFC 2027 launch on schedule with clear digital asset rules

Key Risks

  1. Liquidity crisis: Deposit-credit gap (VND2 quadrillion) forcing banks to issue expensive bonds
  2. NIM compression: Banks sacrificing profitability to maintain credit growth
  3. Exchange rate pressure: USD/VND dynamics limiting SBV easing options
  4. Gold price volatility: Vinhomes gold-for-property scheme exposed to gold price swings
  5. Policy overreach: Aggressive anti-speculation measures dampening genuine demand

  1. SBV open market operations — Daily liquidity injection levels
  2. Interbank rates — VNIBOR movement (last: 7.08% 3M in April)
  3. Vinhomes gold-for-property uptake — First customer registrations
  4. Hanoi resale curb implementation — Detailed guidance from city authorities
  5. VIFC licensing framework — Any announcements from VIFC-HCMC team
